info.name: VectorPath
info.comment: Extends the Vector class with support for generating custom paths.

description.p: VectorPath provides support for parsing SVG styled path strings.
The generated path can be placed with the X and Y fields and sized with the Width and Height fields. These are applied as a post-transform, so the authored path commands are never modified.

action.name: Flush
action.comment: Validates writable command edits and invalidates the generated path.

description.p: After editing the native writable Commands span, call Flush to validate coordinate modes and refresh parent-size dependencies. InvalidValue rejects unsupported masks or non-finite offset magnitudes. Tiri reads Commands as a copied typed array; assign edited entries to that array and assign the array back to Commands before flushing.

result.error: A value has not passed validation

method.name: AddCommand
method.comment: Add one or more commands to the end of the path sequence.
method.prototype: ERR vp::AddCommand(OBJECTPTR Object, std::span<const struct PathCommand> Commands)

input.param: Array of commands to add to the path.

description.p: This method will add a series of commands to the end of a Vector's existing path sequence. The commands must be provided as a sequential array. Option masks are checked against the supported absolute operands.
Calling this method will also result in the path being recomputed for the next redraw.

result.error: A coordinate-mode mask or offset magnitude is invalid.

method.name: GetCommand
method.comment: Retrieve a specific command from the path sequence.
method.prototype: ERR vp::GetCommand(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Index, struct PathCommand ** Command)

input.param: The index of the command to retrieve.
The requested command will be returned in this parameter.

description.p: Calling GetCommand() will return a direct pointer to the command identified at Index. The pointer will remain valid for as long as the VectorPath is not modified. Returned coordinates retain authored offset magnitudes and their Option mask. In Tiri the returned structure is read-only; clone it and submit edits through SetCommand.

method.name: RemoveCommand
method.comment: Remove at least one command from the path sequence.
method.prototype: ERR vp::RemoveCommand(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Index, INT Total)

input.param: The index of the command to remove.
The total number of commands to remove, starting from the given Index.

description.p: This method will remove a series of commands from the current path, starting at the given Index. The total number of commands to remove is indicated by the Total parameter.

field.name: Commands
field.comment: Direct pointer to the PathCommand array.

description.p: In C++, read the Commands field to obtain a direct pointer to the PathCommand array. This allows the path control points to be modified directly, but it is not possible to resize the path. After making changes to the path, call Flush to register the changes for the next redraw.
This field can also be written at any time with a new array of PathCommand structures. Doing so will clear the existing path, if any.
Options preserves authored offset magnitudes using the PCO bits. Tiri returns a copied typed array; edit its entries and assign the array back to Commands to replace the authored commands.

field.name: Height
field.comment: Scales the path to a fixed or scaled height.

description.p: Setting Height scales the computed path on the vertical axis so that its bounding box matches the supplied height. Scaled values are relative to the height of the parent viewport. The path is scaled about its top edge, after which Y placement is applied. If Height is not set, the path keeps its natural height.
Height behaves in the same way as Width on the vertical axis. Negative values flip the path, so that it spans from Y + Height to Y. Refer to Width for further details.

field.name: PathLength
field.comment: Calibrates the user agent's distance-along-a-path calculations with that of the author.

description.p: The author's computation of the total length of the path, in user units. This value is used to calibrate the user agent's own distance-along-a-path calculations with that of the author. The user agent will scale all distance-along-a-path computations by the ratio of PathLength to the user agent's own computed value for total path length. This feature potentially affects calculations for text on a path, motion animation and various stroke operations.
PathLength is always relative to the authored path. It is not adjusted when the path is sized by the Width and Height fields.

field.name: Sequence
field.comment: A sequence of points and instructions that will define the path.

description.p: The Sequence is a string of points and instructions that define the path. It is based on the SVG standard for the path element d attribute, with additional Kōtuku features. Commands are case sensitive: uppercase commands use absolute coordinates and lowercase commands use relative coordinates.
The following commands are supported:
description.pre: M: Move To L: Line To V: Vertical Line To H: Horizontal Line To Q: Quadratic Curve To T: Quadratic Smooth Curve To C: Curve To S: Smooth Curve To A: Arc Z: Close Path
description.p: The use of lower case characters will indicate that the provided coordinates are relative (based on the coordinate of the previous command).
To terminate a path without joining it to the first coordinate, omit the Z from the end of the sequence.

In uppercase M, L, H, V, Q, T, C and S commands, prefix any explicit coordinate with ~ to measure inward from its parent's right edge (X) or bottom edge (Y). Arc A endpoints also support this syntax; radii, angle and flags do not. For example, M 10 0 H ~10 L ~0 ~0 Z follows the parent size. Signed finite decimal and exponent values are accepted, including ~0, ~-10 and ~1e2; whitespace between the marker and number is invalid. Percentages, expressions and offsets in lowercase commands are not supported. Values are not clamped.

Reference dimensions follow VectorRectangle conventions: the parent viewport's view-box dimensions when defined, otherwise its dimensions, with scene page dimensions as fallback. View-box origins are not added. Resolution occurs before bounds, placement and sizing. Leave Width and Height unset to preserve fixed corner radii; explicit sizing scales the entire resolved shape. Parent resizing resolves the authored values again without modifying Commands.

Malformed tokens return Syntax and unsupported roles or non-finite values return InvalidValue. Assignment clears the previous path and retains complete commands preceding the first error, excluding the invalid command.

Reading Sequence returns resolved, post-sizing numeric geometry. Assigning that result creates a fixed snapshot without parent dependencies. SVG export likewise uses standard numeric coordinates. Authored sequences containing ~ are a Kōtuku extension and cannot be passed directly to standard SVG readers.

field.name: TotalCommands
field.comment: The total number of points defined in the path sequence.

description.p: The total number of points defined in the path Sequence is reflected in this field. Modifying the total directly is permitted. Expansion creates zero-initialised entries with no coordinate modes. The maximum is one million entries.

field.name: Width
field.comment: Scales the path to a fixed or scaled width.

description.p: Setting Width scales the computed path on the horizontal axis so that its bounding box matches the supplied width. Scaled values are relative to the width of the parent viewport. The path is scaled about its left edge, after which X placement is applied. If Width is not set, the path keeps its natural width.

Width and Height are independent: if only one is set, the other axis keeps its natural size and the aspect ratio is not preserved. A width of zero collapses the path to a vertical line. Negative values are permitted and will flip the path on the horizontal axis, so that it spans from X + Width to X.
If the natural width of the path is close to zero (for example, a vertical line) then the path cannot be scaled horizontally and Width has no effect.

Only the path geometry is scaled. The stroke width, dash pattern and markers keep their sizes, and the fit is applied to the geometric bounds rather than the stroked bounds. Transforms applied to the vector take effect after the Width is applied.
The path commands remain unchanged, so reading Commands or calling GetCommand returns the authored path. The Sequence field returns the scaled geometry.
When Width is not set, reading it returns the natural width of the path. To return the path to its natural width, set an undefined value (NaN).

field.name: X
field.comment: The left-side of the path. Can be expressed as a fixed or scaled coordinate.

description.p: Setting X moves the computed path so that its left-most boundary aligns with the supplied coordinate. The path commands remain unchanged.
If the path is sized by Width, X places the left edge of the sized path. A negative Width extends the path to the left of X.

field.name: Y
field.comment: The top of the path. Can be expressed as a fixed or scaled coordinate.

description.p: Setting Y moves the computed path so that its top-most boundary aligns with the supplied coordinate. The path commands remain unchanged.
If the path is sized by Height, Y places the top edge of the sized path. A negative Height extends the path above Y.
